messages:
maria: Hey infra team — opened a tiny TF change to provision a hybrid GPU nodepool (reserved + spot) for infer-stage. Can someone do a quick config/secret wiring check? I'm worried about the capacity_reservation block and the KMS key access for node bootstrap. PR: https://git.redwood/infer/ops/+/r1234

josh: quick glance — can you paste the TF snippet and the k8s nodepool manifest here? easier to eyeball.

maria: sure, pasted below.
```hcl
resource "aws_instance" "gpu_node" {
  ami = var.gpu_ami
  instance_type = "g5.48xlarge"
  count = var.reserved_count

  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = "open"
    capacity_reservation_target {
      capacity_reservation_id = aws_ec2_capacity_reservation.cr.id
    }
  }

  tags = {
    "k8s-nodepool" = "infer-stage-gpu"
  }
}

resource "aws_iam_role_policy_attachment" "node_kms" {
  role       = aws_iam_role.node_role.name
  policy_arn = aws_kms_key.node_bootstrap_policy.arn
}
```

k8s manifest:
```yaml
apiVersion: eks.amazonaws.com/v1
kind: Nodegroup
metadata:
  name: infer-stage-gpu
spec:
  instanceTypes:
    - g5.48xlarge
  scalingConfig:
    minSize: 0
    maxSize: 20
    desiredSize: 4
  taints:
    - key: "gpu"
      value: "true"
      effect: "NO_SCHEDULE"
  labels:
    workload: "inference"
  capacityType: "SPOT" # will rely on reserved fallback
```

maria: notes: we set capacityType to SPOT in the nodegroup so autoscaler can scale spot nodes; reserved instances are created by TF for baseline. Concern: does node bootstrap get access to decrypt secrets from KMS (we use kms key in ssm param and secrets manager) without overly broad role? Also need advice on autoscaler annotation to prefer tainted gpu nodes for certain pods.

carla: two quick things: 1) capacity_reservation_target requires the reservation to be in same AZ as instance — TF should ensure cr.az = instance.az. 2) node_role -> KMS policy: rather than attach key ARN as policy_arn directly, use a resource policy on the KMS key granting the node_role decrypt access — that avoids giving the role blanket kms:ListKeys. Example snippet in PR comments.

oliver: also watch spot interruption behavior — set autoscaler expander and pod disruption budgets. If reserved baseline is small, we might get cold starts on fallback. Maybe set NodeGroup capacityType to MIXED and let ASG do allocation? Not all controllers support MIXED on managed nodegroups.

josh: @maria for autoscaler, add annotation on the nodegroup: cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict: "false" for gpu critical pods? Actually we set pod annotations not nodegroup. For taint + toleration: add toleration to inference daemonset and set priorityClass to system-node-critical? be careful.

infra-bot: Deploy-check: terraform plan for PR r1234 completed with warnings: 1) resource aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.node_kms references aws_kms_key.node_bootstrap_policy which has a resource-based policy allowing principal '*' — please scope principals. 2) capacity_reservation_specification will fail if reservation doesn't exist in target AZ.

maria: thanks — i'll update TF to create CR in each AZ and conditionally attach based on var.az_count. For KMS I'll move to key policy and add least privilege. Also adding nodegroup mixed instance types to let fallback to on-demand g5.12xlarge if 48x not available.

tara: I can review the PR after those changes. quick nit: rename tag to "nodepool=infer-stage-gpu" so we can query by tag filters. :white_check_mark:

maria: awesome — pushing updates now. will ping when ready for review. :pray:

josh: lgtm for the approach. small TODO: add terraform import instructions in PR description for existing capacity reservations if any.

maria: noted — will add. thanks everyone.
